slides.title: Microsoft Plugin Architecture: reuse the core, govern each host
slides.notes:
Bottom line: standardize skills and MCP, then govern compatibility and ownership for each host.

Cowork uses a Microsoft 365 app package. Declarative agents use MCP or REST API actions. GitHub Copilot uses plugin packages with portable and client-specific parts.

Reuse skill logic and MCP configuration where tested. Keep authentication, manifests, discovery and client-only components inside each host package.

REST API actions remain supported in declarative agents. Agent Plugins 1.0 adds portability, while legacy GitHub Copilot plugins continue to load.

Assign one owner per capability and service. Publish a host compatibility matrix, version each package, and add routes only when demand justifies lifecycle cost.

items.text: Decision: Standardize skills and MCP; govern compatibility and ownership per host.

slides.title: 1. Choose the host route
slides.notes: Evidence: the three selected official sources, retrieved 2026-10-06. Decision implication: name the host and package contract for every portfolio item; do not describe these routes as interchangeable.

items.text: 1. Choose the host route
Cowork uses a Microsoft 365 app package. Declarative agents use MCP or REST API actions. GitHub Copilot uses plugin packages with portable and client-specific parts.
Claims
Three host routes use different delivery contracts: Cowork uses Microsoft 365 app packages; declarative agents use MCP or API actions; GitHub Copilot uses plugin packages.
Cowork packages skills and connectors in a standard Microsoft 365 app package.
Microsoft 365 declarative agents support MCP and REST API plugins as in-agent actions; REST API tools are defined in the plugin manifest.

slides.notes: Evidence: Cowork skill portability, declarative-agent MCP/API behavior, and GitHub Agent Plugins portability and legacy support. Interpretation: the reusable layer should be separated from host packaging and operations.

items.text: 3. Preserve supported paths
